topic.title: Marginal capacity utility in the strongest joint model
topic.question: Under the unchanged inputs, history policy and training protocol, can capacity reduction or reallocation preserve the frozen joint best's click AUC while lowering measured prediction cost?
topic.hypothesis: The inherited joint history-compression and task-conditioned representation may contain capacity whose removal preserves predictive information. This is unverified; the earlier capacity topic at a weaker starting point does not establish transfer. First compare simple capacity reductions with the unchanged joint best, then use matched-parameter reallocations and replacement controls to distinguish useful allocation from size or compute effects. Freeze an AUC preservation criterion before screening, measure parameters, training wall time and inference time under matched conditions, and reserve budget for attribution and repeated comparisons. A reproducible AUC loss or no measured cost reduction rejects a candidate's utility; failure across the bounded reductions limits this hypothesis without proving all capacity necessary. Keep the shared baseline and current compression best as utility references. Preserve all input and mask restrictions and training exposure. Seed variation and runtime noise are alternative explanations, and repeated seeds alone do not establish a mechanism. Freeze selection before any authorized withheld assessment.
